metadata.source_authority: CMS / NCHS Official Guidelines for Coding and Reporting

guideline_index.section: Section I.C.1.d - Infectious and Parasitic Diseases: Sepsis
guideline_index.title: Sepsis as Principal Diagnosis
guideline_index.citation: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines FY2026, Section I.C.1.d.1.a
guideline_index.summary_rationale: If sepsis is present on admission (POA) and meets the definition of principal diagnosis, the systemic infection code (A41.-) should be sequenced first, followed by localized infection codes as secondary diagnoses.

guideline_index.title: Severe Sepsis Coding & Organ Dysfunction
guideline_index.citation: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines FY2026, Section I.C.1.d.1.b
guideline_index.summary_rationale: The coding of severe sepsis requires a minimum of 2 codes: first a code for the underlying systemic infection, followed by a code from subcategory R65.2 (Severe sepsis) and associated acute organ dysfunction codes.

guideline_index.title: Pneumonia with Sepsis Sequencing
guideline_index.citation: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines FY2026, Section I.C.10.a
guideline_index.summary_rationale: When pneumonia is localized and secondary to systemic sepsis, Pneumonia is classified as a Major Complication or Comorbidity (MCC) and sequenced as a secondary diagnosis.

guideline_index.section: Section I.C.10 - Chronic Obstructive Pulmonary Disease
guideline_index.title: COPD with Acute Exacerbation
guideline_index.citation: ICD-10-CM Official Guidelines FY2026, Section I.C.10.5.a
guideline_index.summary_rationale: Code J44.1 is assigned when COPD is documented with an acute exacerbation. If an infection such as pneumonia is also present, sequence based on the principal diagnosis rules.
